newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The anti-graft court yesterday ordered the 90-day suspension of Senator Miriam Defensor-Santiago for graft charges filed against her while she was immigration commissioner. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Court of Appeals yesterday removed the last stumbling block to the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Speaker Jose de Venecia has succeeded in convincing 35 senior administration-backed congressmen to keep their hands off current efforts to amend the 1987 Constitution and focus their attention instead to more important economic legislation. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The visiting International Monetary Fund panel yesterday urged the administrtaion's economic managers to scale down the country's gross domestic product growth target this year to 6.3 percent from the current target range of 7.1 to 7.8 percent, sources said. (BULLETIN/STAR)
- The Board of Investments will strictly implement a law requiring all Board of Investments-registered firms to divest 10 percent of its outstanding shares to the public. (CHRONICLE/BULLETIN)

- The Department of Finance is opposing the Board of Investments' bid to extend the tax breaks to firms importing capital equipment for another five years after its scheduled phase-out by 1999. (TODAY/TIMES)
